ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: The Act on Reporting and Using Specific Financial Transaction Information (Act No. 6516, as amended) requires all regulated financial institutions to conduct customer due diligence and identify the beneficial owners of every legal person. The Real Name Financial Transactions Guarantee Act (Act No. 4861) prohibits anonymous financial transactions and mandates real name identification for accounts and deposits. The Foreign Investment Promotion Act (Act No. 16898) requires reporting of foreign investment by a foreign-invested entity such as a Yuhan Hoesa. Beneficial ownership data is maintained by the reporting financial institution and is accessible on demand by the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) and law-enforcement counter-terrorism authorities; there is no publicly searchable UBO registry. Regulatory guidance under Financial Services Commission Notice on AML/CFT internal controls imposes a 25% ownership threshold and a control-based definition of beneficial owner.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the Corporate Shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company Registrar in the country of origin (e.g., Companies House, State Business Registry)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path (origin is Apostille Convention member): notarize the certificate with a local civil-law or common-law notary, obtain an apostille from the origin's designated competent authority (e.g., Secretary of State or Ministry of Justice), then present directly to the Korean registry and commercial banks. Consular Legalization path (origin is not an Apostille member): notarize the certificate, have it authenticated by the origin's Ministry of Foreign Affairs, legalize it by the Embassy/Consulate of the Republic of Korea in the origin country, then present it. These two paths are parallel alternatives and must not be combined sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing of the Corporate Shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company Registry or Tax Authority in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille members: notarize, apostille, then use directly in Korea. Non-members: notarize, authenticate at the origin Ministry of Foreign Affairs, legalize at the Korean Embassy/Consulate, then use in Korea. These paths are mutually exclusive alternatives and never sequential.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution or Power of Attorney appointing the Korean incorporation agent and opening the registered office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the corporate shareholder or its law firm
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille members: board minutes notarized by local notary, apostilled by the competent authority, then accepted by Korean registry and banks. Non-members: notarized board minutes authenticated by origin's Ministry of Foreign Affairs and consular legalized by the Korean diplomatic mission. The two paths are independent and not to be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association / Memorandum / Charter of the corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company Registry or notarial archive in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille members: notarized copy apostilled by the origin's competent authority and submitted directly. Non-members: notarized copy, authenticated by the origin MFA, consular legalized by the Korean Embassy. Apostille and consular legalization are alternative, not cumulative.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter for the corporate shareholder or ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: A commercial bank that maintains the shareholder's settlement account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille members: bank officer's signature notarized and the letter apostilled; then submitted to the target Korean bank. Non-members: notarize the bank officer's signature, authenticate at the origin MFA, legalize at the Korean Embassy/trade. The two regimes are parallel; no sequential chaining.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Copy of Identity Document of each UBO, Director and Authorized Signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Civil Notary in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille members: notarize the photocopy, apostille it, and file directly. Non-members: notarize, authenticate at origin MFA, obtain Korean consular legalization, and file. These are exclusive alternatives; never run an apostille then a consular legalization on the same document.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Every corporate shareholder, individual UBO, director, officer, and authorized signatory must be screened, at onboarding and continuously, against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, the US OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, the UK HM Treasury Sanctions List, and the Republic of Korea's own designated terrorist and sanctions list administered by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Financial Services Commission. The screening must also cover enhanced due diligence for politically exposed persons (PEPs), their immediate family members, and known close associates; each PEP exposure requires a documented source of wealth and source of funds, senior management approval, and continuous transaction monitoring. Any confirmed or inconclusive hit must be escalated to the AML compliance officer, reported to the Korea FIU under the Financial Transactions Report Act, and the onboarding must be blocked until a negative or mitigated finding is documented.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registry Office (i-Registry / i-reg.go.kr)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Yuhan Hoesa is the mandatory legal form suffix and must appear at the end of the name in Hangul script. All Korean registered company names must be written in Hangul; foreign brand names and personal names must be rendered by standard phonetic transliteration rules of the National Institute of Korean Language. The four-tier naming convention is: (1) the distinctive trade mark or brand name; (2) the business purpose descriptor; (3) the obligatory Yuhan Hoesa suffix; and (4) an optional non-registered English trade name noted in parentheses. Names that are identical or misleadingly similar to existing enterprises, governmental authorities, public institutions, universities, or indicate a false business scope will be rejected.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 14 days of receiving the official rejection memo from the Registry Office, the applicant or its licensed Korean incorporation agent may file a written appeal with the same Registry through an authorized judicial scrivener, attaching the proposed name, a comparative list of existing identical or similar names, and the legal basis for distinctiveness. The Registry must decide within two weeks. If the appeal is dismissed, the applicant may institute an administrative suit in the competent district court under the Administrative Litigation Act, or may instead modify the name by adding a distinguishing geographic or business descriptor and re-apply through i-reg.go.kr without losing priority, provided the original rejection ground is fully remedied.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, as amended, Articles 287-1 through 287-45 (Limited Liability Company or Yuhan Hoesa) together with the applicable registration provisions of the Commercial Registration Act; Foreign Investment Promotion Act, as amended, Articles 2, 5 and 6 for foreign shareholders; and the Supreme Court Registration Fee Schedule for court charges.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Company Registration Division of the Local District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office, administered through the Supreme Court Internet Registration Service (IROS); for Seoul, the Seoul Central District Court Registry, Civil Affairs and Family Registration Department.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Yuhan Hoesa (limited liability company) under the Commercial Registration Act, together with the notarized Articles of Incorporation, the bank certificate of paid-up capital, director and auditor consents, and the registered office proof.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is prescribed for a Yuhan Hoesa. However, each member's contribution must be fully paid or the in-kind contribution fully delivered before incorporation. Cash contributions must be deposited into a blocked pre-registration escrow account opened in the provisional name of the company; the bank holds the funds and may release them only against the court-issued certificate of incorporation or on lawful abandonment of the formation. For a typical initial capital of KRW 10,000,000, the total official registry fees, registration tax, local education tax and court fee approximate USD 45 at current exchange rates.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION OF THE FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF YUHAN HOESA (LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY). The undersigned directors, constituting the entire Board of Directors of Yuhan Hoesa (the 'Company'), acting under Articles 287-1 through 287-45 of the Korean Commercial Act and the Company's notarized Articles of Incorporation, hereby convene and unanimously adopt the following resolutions in order to perfect the Company's formation and to enable its operations with full statutory validity: 1. Subscription of Contributions and Paid-in Capital. The board ratifies the subscription of all contribution units, totalling KRW [amount] (the 'Paid-in Capital'), subscribed by founding members, and confirms that such contributions have been fully funded prior to registration as required by law. The board accepts the paid-in capital and directs the Representative Director to retain it in the Company's blocked pre-registration account until the registry issues the certificate of incorporation. 2. Registered Office. The board adopts as the sole registered office of the Company the address specified in the Articles of Incorporation, which is located within the territorial jurisdiction of the competent District Court Registry; directs that all official notices be served at that address; and authorizes the execution of the office lease and administrative contracts. 3. Banking and Payment Infrastructure. The board authorizes the opening of corporate settlement, treasury and payroll accounts with the Company's financial institution; appoints the Representative Director and the Chief Financial Officer as joint authorized signatories; and instructs the establishment of merchant accounts with Amazon Pay, Stripe and other payment gateways to collect online sales proceeds. Any contract involving indebtedness above KRW [threshold] requires prior board authorization. 4. Statutory Officers and Corporate Governance. The board appoints [name] as Representative Director and Chief Executive Officer, [name] as Director and Company Secretary, and [name] as Auditor or Audit Officer if the Company reaches the statutory threshold, each to serve until the next ordinary meeting of members and to exercise all duties set by law. 5. Licensing and Governance Ratification. The board ratifies the acts of the founders, counsel, notaries and agents in connection with incorporation, capital deposit, name reservation, registration filing and tax pre-filings; directs management to apply for the factory establishment permit, child product safety confirmation, fire safety certificate, environmental emission report and occupational safety approvals before commencing laser manufacturing; and confirms that this resolution is an enforceable corporate act. Adopted and effective as of the date first written above, by unanimous consent of all directors.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea, accessible via the Home Tax Service (HTS) electronic portal at www.hometax.go.kr
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign non-resident entity must first appoint a domestic tax representative (Korean tax agent) if it has no fixed place of business in Korea. The representative or the entity must submit an application for business registration (사업자등록신청) to the district tax office having jurisdiction over the place of business or the representative's address. Supporting documents include the certificate of foreign corporate registration or equivalent constitutional documents, articles of incorporation, proof of the domestic place of business or agent appointment, and identification documents of the representative. The NTS issues a Business Registration Number (사업자등록번호), which serves as both the Korean Tax Identification Number (TIN) and the VAT registration number for a business. The registration must be completed before commencing taxable business activities, and modifications to business details must be reported to the district tax office.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None (Korean tax law does not provide a check-the-box or hybrid mismatch election equivalent to that of the United States; a Korean Yuhan Hoesa is automatically treated as a domestic corporation subject to entity-level corporate income tax on worldwide income. Certain consolidated tax filing rules apply only to qualifying domestic corporate groups with NTS approval.)

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general mandatory registration threshold exists; any person supplying taxable goods or services in Korea in the course of business, regardless of turnover, must register for VAT. For small businesses meeting simplified taxation requirements, special rules apply, but registration is still mandatory once supplies commence.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All VAT-registered businesses must issue electronic tax invoices (전자세금계산서) through the NTS Home Tax Service, either via the web portal, a dedicated API (e-invoice integration), or NTS-certified ERP/personalized billing programs. Electronic tax invoices must be transmitted to the NTS by the end of the day following the tax invoice issue date. There is no pre-clearance or real-time fiscal stamping model for standard domestic sales, but the NTS operates real-time electronic transaction reporting (현금영수증 의무 발급) for cash receipts and for transactions with end-consumers; credit card transaction data and cash receipts are reported to the NTS by approved payment intermediaries. Anti-fraud measures rely on mandatory electronic issuance, automated cross-matching of purchase and sales invoices, and e-invoice data validation through the Home Tax Service APIs.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is applied to the export of goods under Article 21 of the former VAT Act and the current Value-Added Tax Act, where goods are delivered to a foreign buyer and removed from Korea, or supplied to ships/aircraft engaged in international navigation. Qualifying cross-border services include those performed or used outside Korea, certain international transportation services, and other services explicitly classified as exported services. The specific supply of laser-cut 3D wooden puzzles qualifies as a zero-rated export of goods when the goods are physically exported by a Korean seller under an export customs declaration and title passes to a foreign customer. Sales via online marketplaces or payment gateways must still be supported by formal export customs clearance documents unless the goods are supplied through an overseas fulfillment center where the export movement is evidenced by customs reports. Offshore digital services provided by a Korean supplier to a non-resident may also qualify as zero-rated foreign services if the place of supply is outside Korea and the consideration is received from a non-resident, subject to documentary evidence requirements.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Korea Customs Service Export Declaration (수출신고필증 / Export Declaration Certificate) evidencing the completed customs clearance from Korea
Bill of Lading (B/L) or Air Waybill (AWB) showing the Korean seller as shipper and the foreign buyer as consignee
Commercial Invoice and packing list in the name of the Korean exporting entity
Evidence of consideration received from abroad, including bank remittance documentation, overseas payment settlement statements, or international credit card settlement records

Foreign exchange earnings certificate or foreign exchange transaction report issued by a foreign exchange bank under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, showing receipt of export proceeds within the statutory period
Contract or purchase order from the overseas buyer evidencing the commercial terms and destination
Shipping manifest, container tracking report, or delivery confirmation for goods moved through an overseas fulfillment center or customs-bonded warehouse
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Korean tax authority may scrutinize export documentation under the framework of the International Tax Adjustment Act and the Punishment of Tax Evasion Act. If zero-rated export transactions are found to be fictitious, unsupported by physical export proof, or lacking repatriation of foreign exchange within the mandatory period without a valid extension, the NTS will retroactively reverse the zero-rating, impose the standard 10% VAT plus an additional tax of 10% of the unpaid tax for non-reporting, and apply penalty taxes up to 40% of the unpaid amount for unjustified underreporting or fraudulent claims. Officers or entities involved in fraudulent export documentation may be subject to criminal penalties including imprisonment up to three years or a fine not exceeding three times the evaded tax under the Punishment of Tax Evasion Act. The NTS may also impose the export bond-related customs enforcement and withholding penalties where foreign exchange obligations are violated.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK), acting jointly with the Ministry of Economy and Finance as the foreign exchange administration authority under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act; domestic foreign exchange banks are delegated the day-to-day verification, reporting and settlement execution.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea operates a predominantly liberalised current account system but maintains a managed/report-based capital account. For an ordinary trade and manufacturing Yuhan Hoesa, cross-border trade payments, service fees, royalties and routine dividend remittances are freely executable through a licensed foreign exchange bank once the underlying transaction is substantiated, reflecting current-account convertibility for visible and invisible trade. Capital-account transactions, including inbound foreign direct investment, external equity injections, inter-company loans and cross-border derivatives, are subject to pre-notification or filing with the Ministry of Economy and Finance and the Bank of Korea under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. The KRW is not fully offshore-convertible; offshore non-deliverable KRW positions are restricted and physical KRW cannot be freely transferred across the border beyond the statutory declaration threshold. For non-resident owners, the main remittance hurdle is evidencing the foreign-investment notification and local tax clearance; once the operation is properly registered, profit remission is permissible after dividend resolution, audit/tax filing and bank verification. No mandatory expatriation of export receipts applies, but statistical reporting and collection-period obligations still apply.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: South Korea does not require exporters to surrender foreign-currency export receipts to the central bank. Exporters may deposit export proceeds in licensed foreign-currency accounts or convert them to KRW at a domestic bank. Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, export proceeds must be received within two years from the date of the export declaration unless an extension is granted; the handling bank must be notified of each receipt and settlement. There is no fixed mandatory conversion ratio, and the exporter is free to match USD or KRW liquidity needs with forwards or spot conversion.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account for non-resident direct investment and paid-in capital
Basic Operational Currency Account (KRW and USD multi-currency)
Basic Operational Currency Account with trade finance and LC desk
Capital Escrow Account and FX current account for import/export settlements

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low and legally constrained. Offshore digital EMI platforms such as Revolut Business, Wise Business and Airwallex are not licensed commercial banks in South Korea and cannot open a domestic KRW account for a Yuhan Hoesa or legally process FX transactions for a Korean resident treasury without violating the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. Korean money transfer and payment services must be registered with the Financial Services Commission and related authorities. An EMI may be used only as a supplementary collection rail when settlement is ultimately cleared through a licensed Korean bank, but it cannot serve as the primary account for capital contributions, trade payments, corporate disbursements or FX hedging. The treasury relationship must therefore sit with a tier-1 Korean commercial bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Korean commercial banks generally require statutory directors to appear in person at an authorized branch for first-time corporate account opening, including execution of signed banking mandates and corporate seal registration. A remote consular proxy opening is permitted in limited circumstances for a foreign non-resident director only if the bank's global branch accepts a notarized and apostilled power of attorney, certified passports and corporate documents; however, the opening branch will still conduct a video or telephone KYC interview with the director and locally appointed representative before activating cross-border trade/FX services.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident beneficial owner with no Korean residential address and no local director; KYC flags possible shell-company formation and concealed ownership.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled and notarized articles of incorporation and company register extracts; shareholder registry showing natural-person UBOs; passports of all 25% or more owners; six months of bank statements from the overseas remitting account proving source of wealth; KYC questionnaire; UBO tax identification numbers; and a simple organizational chart linking the Korean entity to the ultimate owners.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade/payment purpose mismatch: the laser puzzle manufacturer uses Amazon Pay and Stripe as target payment rails, but imported laser components and physical exports require customs declarations, causing bank concerns over undocumented cross-border activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Void/provisional commercial invoices; final customs export/import declarations; Amazon and Stripe settlement reports; purchase orders from component suppliers; equipment invoice for the CO2 laser cutter; shipment tracking bills of lading; and a process flow file explaining how each marketplace receipt maps to the entity's trade cycle.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear capital injection source in a low-minimum-capital Korean LLC; the bank fears that the escrow funding may originate from personal savings, crypto exchanges, or third-party unwarranted transfers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed declaration of source of funds; overseas bank account statements in the same UBO name showing the inward remittance; loan agreement, promissory note or director capital call if the contribution is debt-funded; proof of the foreign investment notification filed under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act; and a CPA capital verification certificate after the funds are receipted.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO/director PEP or high-risk jurisdiction citizenship; local AML screening flags trade settlement with third-country suppliers and possible sanctions exposure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid passport and residence status; independent PEP and sanctions screening declarations; UN/OFAC sanctions database check results; legitimate business address and income evidence in the home country; historical transaction records with the third-country supplier; end-user certificates for export goods; and a written corporate undertaking not to route payments through restricted jurisdictions.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route inbound equity via SWIFT MT103 from the UBO or parent company bank to the Yuhan Hoesa Capital Escrow Account at a licensed Korean FX bank. The remittance must carry the inward foreign direct investment/equity acquisition purpose code prescribed by the Bank of Korea reporting rules and a memo line stating Paid-in Capital for Yuhan Hoesa. File the foreign investment notification with the Korean authorities (Invest KOREA/KOTRA or the handling bank) under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act before or at remittance. After credit, obtain the bank's foreign-exchange confirmation, arrange a CPA capital verification if required, and register the foreign-invested enterprise at the National Tax Service and corporate registry before issuing shares.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SWIFT MT103 for open-account supplier remittances supported by invoices and customs declarations. For high-value laser components, issue an irrevocable Commercial Letter of Credit via MT700 with the beneficiary's required shipping documents. For medium-value shipments, use Documentary Collections (D/P or D/A) through the local bank to reduce working capital strain. Every outbound disbursement must be linked to the corresponding customs import entry and purchase order, and the bank will assign the applicable FX purpose code and settle using the interbank rate.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla forward contracts up to one year (renewable) on genuine underlying export/import exposures in KRW/USD, KRW/EUR and KRW/JPY with a licensed domestic FX bank.

Non-deliverable forward (NDF) transactions in KRW are permitted only through licensed domestic KRW NDF channels and require documented genuine exposure; speculative or uncovered NDF positions are not allowed under Korean FX rules.

Cross-currency swaps and interest-rate swaps are permitted only when linked to existing offshore debt, trade finance or commercial funding exposure, and any derivative must be approved by the bank under the real-demand principle; leveraged, unhedged or pure speculative derivative trades are prohibited.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Tax Return and Financial Statements Submission
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: March 31 following the end of the fiscal year (December 31); a filing extension may be granted by the NTS for up to one additional month if audited by a certified tax accountant
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Additional tax of 20% of the unpaid tax if the return is filed late; additional 0.022% per day (8.03% annual) for non-payment; administrative collection procedures and business suspension may follow after repeated failures; criminal penalties up to 3 years imprisonment for willful evasion

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local (Municipal) Business License and Business Activity Renewal Confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local government / Si-Gun-Gu office where the registered business address is located
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No separate annual renewal is required for the business license, but any changes in business location, owners, or key business items must be reported within 30 days; annual verification occurs through municipal tax invoice issuance statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to report changes within 30 days triggers a penalty of up to 3 million KRW (approximately USD 2,200) for the representative; repeated non-compliance may result in administrative closure of the business operation

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Withholding Tax Return and Payment (for employees and resident/non-resident service providers)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Monthly withholding returns are due by the 10th of the following month; if no withholding occurs during the first half-year, a simplified semi-annual return is due by July 10; annual withholding statements are due by March 10 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty equal to 20% of the unpaid withholding tax; additional 0.022% per day interest on delayed payments; if the company fails to withhold, the company itself is jointly liable for the tax owed

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value-Added Tax (VAT) Quarterly Declaration and Payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: First half-year (January 1 – June 30): preliminary return due April 25, final return due July 25; Second half-year (July 1 – December 31): preliminary return due October 25, final return due January 25
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late return penalty of 20% of the tax unpaid; non-declaration of taxable supplies triggers 10% of the unreported tax as penalty; minimum negligence penalty of 500,000 KRW (approximately USD 370) if no tax due but filing not made

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Fixed Asset Tax and Comprehensive Real Estate Holding Tax Annual Assessment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local municipal government (Si-Gun-Gu) and provincial tax authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Fixed asset tax: buildings are taxed in July and October (bills issued June 1 and September 1); land is taxed in September (bill issued August 1); Comprehensive Real Estate Tax for high-value holdings: due December 15
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment interest of 3% for the first month, then 0.75% for each additional month up to 12% maximum; unpaid taxes trigger seizure of movable or immovable property; administrative auction after repeated delinquency

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Registry Audit and Statutory Filing Confirmation (Commercial Registry) – no annual return, but entity records must be kept current
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Korean Commercial Registry (Gu court registration office)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No fixed annual filing is mandated for a Yuhan Hoesa except when changes occur; however, an annual written resolution confirming the financial statements and approval of directors' activities must be documented by the representative director within 15 days prior to the annual shareholders' meeting (which must be held within 90 days after fiscal year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to update the registry when required (change of directors, increase of capital, merger, etc.) results in a non-compliance penalty not exceeding 5 million KRW (approximately USD 3,700); continued failure to maintain proper corporate records can lead to a criminal fine and, in extreme cases, court-ordered dissolution upon creditors' application

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Social Insurance Contribution Filing and Payment (National Pension, National Health Insurance, Employment Insurance, Industrial Accident Compensation Insurance)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Pension Service, National Health Insurance Service (NHIS), Korea Employment Information Service, Korea Workers' Compensation & Welfare Service
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Monthly premium payments are due by the 10th of the following month; annual wage adjustment and end-of-year settlement must be completed by March 10 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Delinquent premiums accrue 3% plus 1% per month in arrears; authorities may issue compulsory collection notices, seize bank accounts, and suspend business operations; criminal penalties apply to intentional failure to enroll employees

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Trade Statistics Filing (if export/import of finished wooden puzzles or raw materials occurs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Korea Customs Service (KCS) via the Korea Trade Statistics Promotion Institute (KTSPI)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Monthly trade data must be filed by the 15th of the following month via the Electronic Data Interchange (EDI) system; no separate annual filing exists beyond the consolidated yearly trade summary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file accurate trade statistics results in a fine of up to 20 million KRW (approximately USD 14,800) or imprisonment up to 3 years if fraudulent; late filing penalties are assessed per day up to 1 million KRW

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory external audit by a certified public accountant (CPA) is compulsory if the company meets any of the following criteria under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies and the Enforcement Decree: (1) Total assets exceed 12 billion KRW (approximately USD 8.9 million); (2) Total revenue exceeds 10 billion KRW (approximately USD 7.4 million) and total assets exceed 7 billion KRW (approximately USD 5.2 million); (3) Revenue exceeds 7 billion KRW (approximately USD 5.2 million) and employee headcount exceeds 300; (4) The company is a limited liability company (Yuhan Hoesa) that has applied for audit registration or voluntarily requested an audit; (5) The company has issued securities to the public or is listed (not applicable here). Also, companies with assets below 12 billion KRW but above 3 billion KRW (approximately USD 2.2 million) may be exempt from mandatory audit but must prepare reviewed financial statements by an independent accountant if requested by the NTS. Small companies with total assets under 3 billion KRW are generally exempt from independent audits unless a shareholder holding at least 10% of equity demands one. For a company engaged in manufacturing (ISIC 3240), the asset and turnover thresholds apply without sector-specific relaxation.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) is mandatory for all companies subject to external audit whose total assets exceed 12 billion KRW (approximately USD 8.9 million). Companies below this threshold may choose K-IFRS or Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (K-GAAP), including the simplified accounting standards for SMEs (SME Accounting Standards) prescribed under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies. If the company becomes subject to a statutory audit, K-IFRS or K-GAAP (with full consistency) must be applied; internal management accounting records must be kept on an accrual basis and in conformity with the pertinent standards.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the Commercial Act and the Act on Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Transaction Information (Anti-Money Laundering Act), a Yuhan Hoesa must maintain a register of ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) at its registered office. There is no standalone annual confirmation filing to a central UBO registry, but the entity must keep the register continuously updated. Any transfer of shares that changes the UBO, or any change in the controlling shareholder's details, must be recorded in the corporate register and reported to the NTS as part of the annual corporate tax return. The NTS may require submission of a 'Beneficial Owner Disclosure' within 30 days from any ownership shift if the entity engages in foreign currency transactions. For the financial year-end, the company must hold at least one regular general meeting of shareholders within 90 days after the end of the fiscal year, at which the UBO details and shareholding structure are ratified minuted. If there is any change in the shareholding percentage of a UBO during the year, the company has a 30-day window from the date of such change to update the share register and to notify the local tax office through the next tax filing. For money laundering risk tier 'Low_Risk_Standard', no special enhanced scrutiny is required beyond the statutory 30-day update rule.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 600 – USD 1,500 per year (inclusive of a standard corporate secretarial service in Seoul metropolitan area; actual cost depends on the chosen legal service provider and address quality)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,500 – USD 12,000 per year for a small to mid-sized manufacturing company preparing reviewed or audited financial statements under K-GAAP / SME Accounting Standards; fees rise to USD 15,000 – USD 30,000 if full K-IFRS audit becomes mandatory

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% top marginal corporate income tax rate under the Corporate Tax Act of Korea (Article 55), applied to taxable income exceeding KRW 300 billion. The progressive national CIT schedule for fiscal years beginning 2023 onwards is: 9% on the first KRW 200 million of taxable income; 19% on the tranche from KRW 200 million to KRW 20 billion; 21% on the tranche from KRW 20 billion to KRW 300 billion; and 24% on income above KRW 300 billion. A local income tax surcharge of 10% is added to the national CIT liability, producing a combined headline marginal rate of 26.4% and a combined rate of 9.9% on the lowest bracket.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday applies to ISIC 3240 (wooden puzzle manufacturing) under normal conditions. However, the effective rate is reduced by the following incentives: (i) the 9% SME preferential bracket on the first KRW 200 million of income; (ii) R&D tax credits under the Special Tax Treatment Control Law (STTCL) Article 10, including an up to 25% credit for qualifying in-house R&D expenses and enhanced rates for new-growth-source technologies; (iii) an up to 30% credit for R&D related to national strategic technologies; (iv) employment tax credits and social insurance premium deductions under STTCL Articles 29-4 and 30-1; (v) foreign-invested enterprise incentives under STTCL Article 121-2 for qualifying investments in Free Economic Zones or Foreign Investment Zones, granting a 100% corporate tax exemption for the first 3 years and a 50% reduction for the next 2 years, provided the foreign investment ratio exceeds 30% and the business qualifies as a high-tech facility; and (vi) facility investment credits for SMEs. After applying these measures, the consolidated effective tax rate for a typical SME can fall below the headline rate. The global minimum top-up tax (Pillar Two) does not currently bind a Korean manufacturing SME below the EUR 750 million threshold.
